data.title: India could gain from Nvidia's weakening competitive edge in AI: William Lee
data.description:
India could emerge as an alternative destination for US chip exports and data centers amid growing uncertainty over the global artificial intelligence (AI) trade, says William Lee, Chief Economist and Managing Director, Global Economic Advisors.

He believes the country's large pool of software engineers and technology talent could also help companies transition from Nvidia chips to alternatives from AMD and Google. However, India will need to build greater trust with the US Commerce Department to attract these opportunities.

Lee says the AI trade is shifting beyond chips and software to financing, a transition he describes as moving from “chips to code and now to credit”. Nvidia's growing role in financing hyperscalers and startups has added to investor concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom.

He believes the resulting market turmoil could create opportunities for Nvidia's competitors and give India a chance to strengthen its position in the global AI supply chain.

Is this a buying opportunity?[/ques][ans]The focus of artificial intelligence (AI) went from chips to code and now to credit. That is the nexus of where Nvidia has been shifting. It was the key chip supplier, maintaining its chip monopoly. Now, with credit, it is financing many of the hyperscalers and startups that are selling and reselling compute power. That has been the heart of the AI trade, and that is also the heart of where the anxiety and uncertainty is. All of these anxieties represent not only a buying opportunity for a lot of companies, especially Nvidia's competitors, but also a huge opportunity for India. This is a place where India can shine in perhaps accelerating the deterioration and the destruction of Nvidia's moat that has protected it and allowed competitor chips to come into the AI chip network.[/ans][/faq]

data.title: ESDS Software clarifies on Sydney AI factory reports; stock extends losses
data.description:
Shares of ESDS Software Solutions Ltd. erased its early gains on Monday, November 23, after the company clarified that its Sydney AI factory project remains on schedule, with all 8,208 NVIDIA B300 GPUs installed and undergoing final testing.

The company said the entire capacity at the facility has been contracted to customers on a take-or-pay basis, with handover expected by mid-December 2026. Billing is scheduled to begin in January 2027.

In a clarification on its agreement with Sharon AI and the Sydney project, ESDS said the delivery timeline had been revised by mutual agreement with the partner. The revised schedule is also in line with the timeline Sharon AI disclosed alongside its quarterly results on November 16. ESDS said it opted to complete testing of the entire GPU cluster before taking handover.

The company said the revised schedule would not increase its costs, as payments to Sharon AI and corresponding receipts from customers will begin only after the cluster is accepted.

It added that the deposit placed with Sharon AI is refundable if the partner fails to meet its contractual delivery obligations.

ESDS said its financial commitment to Sharon AI, as disclosed in its prospectus, stands at approximately $1.26 billion over 60 months, translating into monthly payments of around $21 million. The amount is based on a fixed rate per GPU per hour for the duration of the contract.

The company clarified that the ₹3,000 crore annual cost mentioned during its November 2 earnings call was an approximation, while the contractual commitment works out to approximately $21 million a month.

On the revenue side, ESDS expects to receive around $30 million per month from customers for the Sydney project, against payments of approximately $21 million to Sharon AI. This would leave about $9 million a month before operating expenses and taxes.

Based on the contractual terms, the company currently estimates monthly profit after tax of around $4-5 million, translating into a margin of approximately 14–17% of revenue.

ESDS said the entire capacity of the Sydney facility has been contracted to customers under take-or-pay agreements. This means customers are required to pay for the committed capacity irrespective of actual utilisation.

The company added that the duration and exit provisions of customer agreements are aligned with its contract with Sharon AI, limiting its exposure to the risk of low utilisation. Customers have also made upfront payments, it said, while their identities remain confidential under contractual terms.

The company further clarified that it had placed a cash deposit of $140 million, equivalent to ₹1,336 crore, with Sharon AI in May 2026 instead of providing letters of credit. It said no additional letter of credit or bank guarantee is outstanding or required.

According to ESDS, the deposit was funded through a $140 million advance received from customers and did not require the use of its own cash. The amount will be adjusted against service fees over the contract period and is classified as an advance to vendor.

The customer advances reflected in the company's balance sheet as of September 30, 2026, include amounts received before March 31, 2026, which were disclosed in its prospectus, as well as the $140 million advance used to fund the deposit with Sharon AI.

ESDS said the earlier advances remain unutilised in the group's bank accounts and that it did not receive any significant additional customer advances during the September quarter.

On its role in the project, ESDS said Sharon AI owns the hardware and data centre capacity, while the company will provide customers with a managed service covering cluster operations, round-the-clock network and security monitoring, model training and GPU-as-a-Service.

These services will be offered under a single contract, with ESDS acting as the accountable service provider.

The arrangement allows the company to expand its capacity without making substantial investments in land, buildings or GPU hardware, while continuing to develop its own GPU infrastructure in India.

ESDS said it will inform the stock exchanges once the Sydney AI factory becomes operational and make further disclosures as required under Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulations.

The company also cautioned that payments to Sharon AI and receipts from customers are denominated in US dollars. While currency movements could affect the rupee value of reported revenue, costs and profits, ESDS said they would not change the margin earned in dollar terms. The project timelines and profit estimates remain expectations and are not guaranteed.

ESDS Software Solutions shares opened as much as 2% higher on Monday, November 23, following the clarification.

data.title: Webull HK Launches Korean Stock Trading
data.description:
Offering low commissions, no platform fees and direct trading using US dollars to help investors diversify into the Korean equity market

HONG KONG, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Amid continued growth in the global technology sector, the Korean stock market has attracted increasing attention from international investors in recent years. Webull Securities Limited ("Webull HK"), a subsidiary of Webull Corporation (), the owner of the Webull trading platform, today announced the launch of its Korean stock trading service.

Effective immediately, Hong Kong (SAR) investors can trade stocks listed on the Korea Exchange ("KRX") through Webull HK, with access to both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ markets. The launch further expands Webull HK's global market coverage, enabling Hong Kong investors to access five major equity markets—the United States, Hong Kong (SAR), A-shares, Japan and Korea—through a single platform.

With transparent pricing, direct trading using US dollars and professional market data and analytical tools, Webull HK aims to provide investors with a more comprehensive and cost-effective one-stop global investment experience.

Broad KRX Coverage Expands Asian Asset Allocation Opportunities

The Korean stock market has performed strongly in recent years, attracting sustained inflows of global capital and driving growing investor demand for exposure to the market. The launch of Korean stock trading reflects Webull HK's commitment to meeting investors' demand for overseas growth opportunities and diversified asset allocation. Hong Kong (SAR) investors can now use a single account to trade KRX-listed stocks across the KOSPI and KOSDAQ markets, further advancing the platform's strategy of providing efficient and cost-effective investment services.

Transparent Pricing and Direct Trading Using US Dollars Address Cross-Border Investment Needs

To address the key needs of local investors, Webull HK has introduced a highly competitive pricing and fund management model for Korean stock trading. Commission rates start from 0.08%, with no platform fees, helping investors minimize their overall trading costs. Investors can also use US-dollar balances in their accounts to trade Korean stocks directly, without the need to complete a separate currency conversion process. This simplifies the trading process, improves execution efficiency and provides investors with greater flexibility in managing their funds.

Real-Time Market Data and Professional Charting Tools Support Korean Stock Analysis

Webull HK provides investors with a comprehensive suite of professional market monitoring and analytical tools for Korean stocks. The platform offers real-time streaming quotes and market data, enabling users to monitor movements in the KOSPI and KOSDAQ indices, view market rankings and track KRX-listed stocks.

The platform also offers multi-dimensional fundamental and technical analysis tools, including a range of technical indicators, candlestick charts and intraday charts. These tools help investors analyze individual Korean stocks and identify potential market opportunities. Users who newly activate Korean stock trading permissions can also enjoy complimentary access to standard real-time Korean market data for 30 days.

Strengthening Global Asset Allocation Through a One-Stop Cross-Market Investment Ecosystem

The addition of Korean stock trading further strengthens Webull HK's global market offering. Hong Kong (SAR) investors can now manage investments across the US, HK (SAR), A-shares, Japanese and Korean equity markets through a single account, facilitating diversified cross-market asset allocation.

With an intuitive and user-friendly interface, the Webull app makes it easier for local investors to manage funds and execute trades across multiple markets within a single platform.

Mr. Wang Haichen, Chief Executive Officer of Webull HK, said: "Korea is one of Asia's major capital markets and plays an important role in global industries including semiconductors, AI hardware and advanced manufacturing. The launch of Korean stock trading marks another important step in Webull HK's continued expansion of its global market coverage. With Korean equities joining our existing US stocks, HK (SAR) stocks, A-shares and Japanese stock trading services, Hong Kong (SAR) investors can now access five major equity markets through a single platform, providing them with a broader range of global asset allocation opportunities."

"Looking ahead, we will continue to leverage Webull's global platform capabilities to provide competitive and transparent pricing, innovative trading features and professional investment tools. We remain committed to becoming a one-stop investment platform connecting Hong Kong investors with global capital markets."

About Webull HK

Webull Securities Limited ("Webull HK") is a licensed corporation with the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission, holding SFC Type 1 ("Dealing in Securities"), Type 2 ("Dealing in Futures Contracts"), and Type 4 ("Advising on Securities") licenses, with CE No. BNG700. Since its establishment in 2019, Webull HK has always put investors first, leveraging the technological expertise and proven success of its parent company, Webull Corporation (Nasdaq: BULL), as a leading broker in the US market, while adopting a localized business strategy in Hong Kong. With a highly competitive fee structure and a reliable, secure platform, Webull HK offers trading in a diverse range of assets including US stocks, Hong Kong (SAR) stocks, and options, equipped with institutional grade professional charting tools and real time market data – empowering Hong Kong investors to navigate dynamic global financial markets with confidence. For more information about Webull HK, please visit https://www.webull.hk

About Webull Corporation

Webull Corporation () owns and operates Webull, a leading digital investment platform built on next-generation global infrastructure and AI technologies. Through its global network of licensed brokerages, Webull offers investment services in 19 markets across North America, Asia Pacific, Europe, Africa, and Latin America. Webull serves more than 29 million registered users globally, providing retail and institutional investors with 24/7 access to global financial markets. Users can put investment strategies to work by trading global stocks, ETFs, options, futures, fractional shares, and digital assets through Webull's trading platform, which seamlessly integrates market data and information, its user community, and investor education resources. Learn more at www.webullcorp.com.

data.title: Gold Is Trading Like A Speculative Asset, Says Morningstar Analyst As Price Plunges 17% In 2026
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arnott said one factor contributing to gold’s falling prices is rising interest rates.
  • According to The Kobeissi Letter, gold, which is down about 22% since the start of September, is now on track for its worst 3-month rolling performance since June 2013.
  • Meanwhile, silver prices are down nearly 39% since the start of September, putting them on track for their biggest 3-month rolling decline since 2008.

Gold prices have been highly volatile in recent months, plunging to about $3,502.49 per ounce on Friday, the lowest level since Sept. 2025, while U.S. gold futures for December settled around $3,515.40 per ounce.

The precious metal has tumbled more than 16% year-to-date, with a 22% drop in the last three months alone. Amy C. Arnott, a portfolio strategist at Morningstar, said on Friday that gold has been trading more like a speculative asset rather than a safe haven.

What’s Causing Gold Prices To Tumble?

Arnott said one of the factors contributing to gold’s falling prices is rising interest rates. “If you have higher yields available on bonds and cash, there's less of a reason for investors to take shelter in gold, which doesn't generate any yield or cash flows on a regular basis,” she said in an interview.

“And I would argue that even though gold is traditionally viewed as a safe haven as you said, I think it's becoming more of a speculative asset where you had a lot of people buying while it was on the way up and then when the price started going down, you had more selling pressure,” she said, adding, “So I think that is also part of the reason why it's fallen so much so far this year.”

Gold’s 3-Month Performance Is On Track For Worst Performance Since 1981

According to The Kobeissi Letter, gold, which is down about 22% since the start of September, is now on track for its worst 3-month rolling performance since June 2013.

“This would also mark gold's largest 3-month rolling price decline since 1981.By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold's biggest 3-month drawdown was -22.2%.”

Silver Also Tumbles Amid Selling Pressure

The market commentator said that silver prices are down nearly 39% since the start of September, putting them on track for their biggest 3-month rolling decline since 2008, when prices fell 45.3%. Silver's largest 3-month rolling decline on record was a fall of 63.6% in 1980.

“Gold and silver are experiencing historic selling pressure,” it said in a post on X.

Spot gold was trading at $3,603.70 an ounce at the time of writing, while spot silver was trading at $42.16 an ounce.

What’s Retail Saying About Gold And Silver?

The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD), which tracks the price of gold, was up 2.33% in the overnight session late Sunday after closing down 3.67% on Friday.

Retail sentiment around GLD slipped from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ over 24 hours on Stocktwits.

One user said, “$GLD glory days are over.”

Meanwhile, the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 3% overnight after closing 6.74% lower on Friday.

Retail sentiment around SLV remained in the ‘bullish’ territory over 24 hours.

One user said, “$SLV $GLD we’re going to open red again aren’t we. So much for a hedge against inflation!”

GLD is down nearly 19% year-to-date, while SLV has plunged more than 43% in the same time.

data.title: Leapmotor's Shares Sharply Lower After Third-Quarter Profitability Weakness
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Shares of Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology fell sharply, after the Chinese automaker's gross profit margin declined in the third quarter.

Its shares dropped 14% to 26.18 Hong Kong dollars early Monday, sharper than the benchmark Hang Seng Index's 0.5% fall.

Leapmotor's decline came after the automaker said its gross profit margin fell to 10.9% in the third quarter, compared with 12.6% in the second quarter and 14.5% a year earlier. Higher material and freight costs weighed on profitability.

Jefferies analysts expect a modest recovery in the company's gross profit margin in the fourth quarter, as memory-chip prices remain high, they said in a note.

Leapmotor's third-quarter revenue rose 63% to 31.7 billion yuan, equivalent to $4.75 billion. However, its net profit plunged to 40 million yuan from 150 million yuan a year earlier despite a record delivery volume of 310,052 units during the period. The company attributed its lower net profit to weaker profitability per vehicle.

Like many of its Chinese peers, Leapmotor faces subdued domestic demand. Sales in foreign markets could offset weakness at home, Jefferies analysts said, adding that the company's overseas profitability could strengthen next year.

The company's vehicle production in overseas markets will likely give it an upper hand in hedging against tariff risks compared with its Chinese peers, they added.

data.title: BlackRock and other Bitcoin ETF issuers see $1.79 billion in weekly outflows
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds saw $1.79 billion in net outflows last week. That is the biggest weekly exit in 21 weeks.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the retreat, and it had plenty of company.

The outflows cover the week ending November 20, 2026. The last time weekly redemptions ran this high was back in June.

It also marks the fourth straight week of net outflows for the group.

IBIT took the heaviest hit. On November 19 alone, investors pulled $541.1 million from BlackRock's fund in a single session.

Zoom out to the full month, and the picture gets heavier. Total November outflows across the 12 US spot Bitcoin ETFs are estimated at between $3.47 billion and $3.59 billion through November 20.

IBIT accounts for around 85% of that monthly total.

The rest of the field was not spared. Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC also recorded outflows over the period.

There were a few exceptions. Morgan Stanley's MSBT posted modest inflows on certain days.

The redemptions lined up with a sharp drop in Bitcoin itself. The asset fell below $62,000, touching lows around $61,270.

That move added up to a decline of more than 10% over a seven-day span.

The broader market backdrop has also turned more cautious. Signals from the Federal Reserve on monetary policy have been weighing on risk appetite across assets.

Spot ETFs are a two-way street. When investors buy shares, issuers acquire Bitcoin to back them. When investors redeem, the funds shed Bitcoin, which is why ETF flow data has become a closely watched gauge of institutional sentiment.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024. Their arrival opened a path for advisers, pensions and traditional brokerage clients to get Bitcoin exposure without touching a crypto exchange or a private key.

Since that launch, cumulative net inflows into the funds stand at approximately $52 billion to $53.5 billion. Even after a month of steady selling, the net tally since inception remains firmly positive.

Set against that total, the latest week's $1.79 billion is a minor fraction of the capital the funds have raised. Even the full November estimate of up to $3.59 billion represents a small dent rather than a collapse.

The concentration in IBIT is worth watching closely. BlackRock's fund was the headline success story of the ETF era, and IBIT accounts for around 85% of monthly outflows.

The scattered inflows into Morgan Stanley's MSBT on some days are a reminder that not every allocator is heading for the exits.

The Federal Reserve remains a key variable. Investors appear to be reassessing risk exposure partly in response to policy signals, which means Bitcoin ETF flows may continue to track macro expectations.

The cumulative inflow figure offers the counterweight. Roughly $52 billion to $53.5 billion in net new money since January 2024 points to institutional interest that has not evaporated, even if it is currently taking a breather.

data.title: BHP unveils $17.4 billion plan to double South Australian copper output by 2040
data.description:
Key points:
  • Aims to boost copper output to 650,000 tons by 2040
  • Final investment decision due H1 next year
  • Project relies on government water infrastructure project

By Melanie Burton

BHP , the world's top copper miner, said on Monday it plans to spend up to $17.4 billion to double its South Australian copper production by 2040, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

BHP said it had found an economic path to raise annual copper output to 650,000 metric tons from the region, which it says is the world's second-biggest source of copper.

"We start from a strong position as the world's largest copper producer, with a sector-leading growth pathway that can be funded from existing copper cash flows," Geraldine Slattery, BHP's head of Australian operations, told investors on a site tour, according to prepared remarks supplied by BHP.

"Copper South Australia is a centrepiece of that growth, contributing around a third of the increase to 2035."

When including the value of byproducts such as uranium, silver and gold, BHP said Copper South Australia's output would be close to the equivalent production at the world's largest copper mine, Chile's Escondida.

The growth will underpin BHP's road map to produce 2 million tons of the metal, which is key to electrification, from its global operations by the middle of the next decade.

Slattery said BHP expects global copper demand to grow by 30% by 2040 to more than 45 million tons per year, driven by electrification, digitalisation and AI demand.

BHP, the world's largest listed miner, reaped more value from its copper division than from iron ore, its prior mainstay, for the first time in fiscal 2026.

CHALLENGING REGION

BHP's plan outlines for the first time how it intends to develop the rich but technically complex ore body riven with high radioactivity, after the company had shelved plans in previous decades due to high costs and commodity downturns.

The Copper South Australia operations include its longstanding Olympic Dam mine, and the Carrapateena and Prominent Hill mines, which it acquired from OZ Minerals in 2023, and its 2018 Oak Dam discovery, which BHP has renamed Ankata.

BHP's operations in the region have proven challenging, due to a combination of operational instability, complex metallurgy and external infrastructure constraints such as water and power, UBS said in a note.

As a result, the complex has achieved a low single-digit return on capital employed for many years, only reaching 10% in fiscal 2026 with record-high commodity prices, UBS added.

BHP said it expects the introduction of block caving, which is a type of bulk mining, and two-stage smelting to underpin significantly lower operating costs, with an internal rate of return at 14% to 17%.

As part of the expansion, BHP plans to roughly double the capacity of its uranium processing plant to 5,000 to 6,000 tons a year, which will raise Australia's contribution of uranium to around 10% of global supply.

DESALINATION OPTIONS

BHP's mines sit within the Gawler Craton, an ancient geological structure formed roughly 2 billion years ago, in an increasingly arid region on the fringes of Australia's remote Outback.

The miner uses water from the Great Artesian Basin, which has sparked concerns from traditional owner groups such as the Arabana people. BHP aims to mitigate its use of the artesian water by using a planned 260-megalitre-a-day seawater desalination plant at Cape Hardy on South Australia's Spencer Gulf. That water would need to be piped hundreds of kilometres. The state and federal governments are yet to commit to the project.

The state government is due to make a final investment decision on the Northern Water infrastructure project next year, and the first water from the project is targeted for fiscal 2032.

The planned expansion will also require power upgrades to existing electricity transmission infrastructure, including a 275-kilovolt transmission line from the town of Davenport some 273 km (170 miles) away.

($1 = 1.5117 Australian dollars)

data.title: Development of BHP's Copper South Australia operations
data.description:
BHP , the world's top copper miner, unveiled plans on Monday to double its South Australian copper production by 2040 at a cost of up to $17.4 billion, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

The centrepiece of that plan, Olympic Dam, was intended to become a top-tier growth engine after BHP took over Western Mining Corporation in 2005. There have been multiple expansion concepts since then, but so far none of them has been executed.

1975 - Western Mining Corp discovers the Olympic Dam mineral deposit in the state of South Australia.

1979 - A joint venture is formed with BP Group to develop the project.

1988 - Underground mining starts at an annual rate of 45,000 metric tons of copper, plus byproducts uranium oxide, gold and silver.

1993 - BP exits the project as WMC acquires BP's 49% share.

1995 - After a series of optimisation projects, Olympic Dam is producing 170,000 metric tons a year of copper and associated byproducts. It has conditional approval to increase that to 350,000 tons.

2005 - BHP acquires WMC, and with it Olympic Dam, for about A$9.2 billion.

2009 - BHP, under CEO Marius Kloppers, proposes a giant open-pit expansion and releases a draft environmental impact study, with plans to lift production by about 515,000 tons of copper per year above existing output.

2011 - The proposed expansion receives major approvals. Industry estimates at the time put the project cost at around $30 billion, which would have made it one of the world's largest mining developments.

2012 - BHP shelves the open-pit expansion. Kloppers says the project had become too costly, linking the decision to weaker commodity markets and the need for stricter capital allocation. The estimated capital bill remained around $30 billion.

2017 - BHP confirms it is investigating a brownfield expansion plan for Olympic Dam under CEO Andrew Mackenzie, which would raise production to 450,000 tons per year of copper from the mid-2020s.

2018 - BHP announces the discovery of the Oak Dam West copper-gold-uranium deposit about 65 km (40 miles) southeast of Olympic Dam, after drilling intersects one of the best copper discoveries in Australia in decades.

2019 - BHP's brownfield expansion plan is declared a major development by South Australia.

2020 - Mike Henry takes the helm of the world's biggest miner and BHP abandons the Olympic Dam expansion plan due to high costs. Instead, it focuses on a debottlenecking strategy which backs incremental investments in smelter, refinery and underground mine capacity rather than a multi-decade open-pit project.

2023 - BHP acquires Australian copper miner OZ Minerals for around A$9.6 billion and creates Copper South Australia by combining Olympic Dam with the former OZ Minerals assets, Prominent Hill and Carrapateena, which are in the same region.

2024-2026 - BHP focuses on lifting production across Copper South Australia through smelter expansion studies, mine growth and exploration, as well as integration of the three asset hubs.

2027 - BHP is due to make a final investment decision on the expansion project.

2063 - Planned closure of the operations.

data.title: APL Apollo Tubes shares plunge 10%, Tata Steel falls 4% as Rs 5,825 crore block deal follows acquisition news
data.description:
Shares of APL Apollo Tubes plunged 10 percent in early trade on Monday, November 23, while Tata Steel declined 4 percent after the steelmaker announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo through a transaction that could cost up to Rs 32,266 crore, including a mandatory open offer.

The sharp declines came as 2.77 crore shares of APL Apollo, representing approximately 10 percent of its equity, changed hands in a large block deal worth Rs 5,825 crore at Rs 2,100 apiece. The transaction follows Tata Steel's announcement earlier in the morning that it would acquire shares from an APL Apollo promoter group entity in multiple tranches.

APL Apollo Tubes shares were trading at Rs 1,910 apiece in early trade, down 10 percent from their previous close. Tata Steel shares fell 4 percent to Rs 170.80. The declines took APL Apollo's year-to-date performance to a loss of 0.8 percent, while Tata Steel was down 4.5 percent in 2026. The Nifty 50 has declined approximately 1 percent this year.

At current prices, APL Apollo Tubes commands a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 53,700 crore, compared with Tata Steel's Rs 2.13 lakh crore.

data.title: EU Inks Deals With Indonesia to Cut Tariffs, Catalyze Investment
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

The European Union signed ambitious agreements with Indonesia that eliminate most tariffs on goods between the two sides, aiming to will deliver billions in economic benefits.

Brussels announced the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with Indonesia on Saturday, more than 10 years after negotiations began. The parties also inked an Investment Protection Agreement to encourage bilateral flows.

"EU-Indonesia trade and investment has vast untapped potential," said Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission.

Duties on main EU export products, including meat and dairy, will be removed, while existing tariffs on cars, machinery, chemicals and pharmaceuticals will be cut.

According to Indonesia's Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, about 90% of tariffs on EU-bound exports to the EU will be removed, while others will be gradually reduced over 3 to 15 years or benefit from tariff-rate quotas.

The preferential access is expected to make Indonesian exports--particularly footwear, textiles and processed commodities--more competitive in the European market, it added.

The pacts open "new doors for businesses," bolstering cooperation in sectors like agri-food and advanced manufacturing, said EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič.

With the deals in place, EU shipments to Indonesia are projected to increase by nearly 40% over 15 years, while Indonesian exports of goods and services to the bloc are expected to rise by more than 14%.

"This will boost economic growth," the commission said, projecting that the EU's gross domestic product will be 16 billion euros higher and Indonesia's 27 billion euros higher, or $17.55 billion and $29.62 billion respectively.

Lowered trade barriers and streamlined investment frameworks will unlock opportunities for European businesses and farmers in Indonesia's market of 280 million consumers, the commission said. EU exporters stand to save over $650 million in annual duties.

Another key benefit for the EU is access to Indonesia's vast resources of materials like nickel and cobalt that are used in everything from electric vehicles to jet engines.

The agreement will give manufacturers stable, predictable access to critical resources, strengthening the trading bloc's supply chain against shocks, the commission said.

"It also provides an export duty-free quota for crude palm and palm kernel oil, both of which are strategic inputs for EU industries," it added.

Recent supply-chain disruptions stemming from wars and other shocks have underlined the need for countries to build up resilience via trade alliances and diversification.

The EU has already concluded agreements with Singapore and Vietnam, and is in ongoing trade negotiations with Thailand and the Philippines.

The investment and economic partnerships struck with Indonesia require the European Parliament's consent and Indonesia's internal ratification. They are expected to be provisionally applied in early 2027.

data.description:
• Australia’s Flash Composite PMI fell to 46.1 in November from 48.2 in October, marking the second consecutive month of contraction and the steepest decline in private-sector activity since August 2021.
  • Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 from 49.6, its lowest since December 2024, while Services PMI declined to 46.2 from 48.5, its steepest contraction since November 2023. Output and new orders across the private sector fell at their fastest pace in over five years.
  • Employment and foreign demand declined, while input and output price inflation eased; business sentiment fell to a three-year low.

data.title: South Korea's KOSPI drops 5% as AI fears trigger broader stock sell-off
data.description:
South Korean stocks extended their losses on Monday, with the benchmark KOSPI falling as much as 5.41% intraday as investors retreated from technology and semiconductor shares amid concerns over AI valuations, heavy infrastructure spending and potential U.S. export restrictions.

The KOSPI had already dropped 5.21% on Friday. At an intraday level of 4,606.44, the benchmark was down approximately 21.4% from its November 2 close.

Samsung Electronics fell nearly 6% at one point during Monday's session, while SK hynix also lost around 6%. Over the past month, Samsung Electronics has declined ~20.1%, while SK hynix has lost around 18.1%, reflecting sustained pressure on South Korea's semiconductor sector.

Among other major companies, Samsung Biologics fell 5.61% on Monday, LG Energy Solution declined 3.26%, Hyundai Motor dropped 4.90%, Kia lost 4.42%, KB Financial Group fell 3.87%, Shinhan Financial Group declined 3.94%, and Samsung Life Insurance dropped 4.18%.

The sell-off followed Friday's sharp decline in U.S. technology and semiconductor stocks, as investors questioned the returns on heavy AI infrastructure spending and grew concerned about tighter U.S. semiconductor export restrictions.

South Korean authorities are preparing a 10T won ($6.8B) stock-market stabilization fund to curb the sell-off and restore investor confidence. The government will also ease restrictions on listed companies’ daily share-buyback orders for three months from November 24, while regulators step up surveillance of illegal short selling and monitor margin loans and potential forced liquidations.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Monday that South Korea's economy could grow in the upper-3% range next year if current trends continue, citing strong exports and investment gradually supporting domestic demand. Consumer inflation is also expected to ease in 2027 as global oil prices stabilize.

However, Lee warned that AI regulation, geopolitical tensions, rising global interest rates, and semiconductor-sector volatility remain key risks. Given South Korea's reliance on chip exports, prolonged weakness in technology demand could weigh on the broader economy.

South Korea-focused ETFs came under significant pressure in November. The Direxion Daily MSCI South Korea Bull 3X ETF plunged 54.10% through November 20, while the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF and xETFs Korea AI Semiconductor ETF fell 26.90% and 24.89%, respectively.

Among broad-market funds, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF declined 18.70%, while the Franklin FTSE South Korea ETF lost 18.08%. The Matthews Korea Active ETF dropped 18.82%, and the PLUS Korea Manufacturing Core Alliance Index ETF fell 23.07%. The PLUS Korea Defense Industry Index ETF recorded a comparatively smaller decline of 13.51%.

data.title: Indonesia says 24 killed in factory blaze as rescuers search for dozens missing
data.description:
Indonesia confirmed on Monday the deaths of 24 people in a fire that tore through a factory at the weekend, as rescuers braved unstable structures in the burned wreckage in the search for about 30 people still missing.

Authorities were still investigating the cause of the fire, which broke out on Saturday evening in one building of the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande in Banten province, about an hour's drive from the capital Jakarta.

Said Iqbal, a presidential adviser on labour issues, told reporters 24 people had died, adding implementation of safety protocols was being assessed and that he would summon the factory's chief executive.

Preliminary reports indicated the fire may have been caused by an air-conditioner short circuit, Said added.

The factory is owned by United Family Food, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The firm employs about 5,000 people overall and is a major supplier of consumer goods to the domestic market, with four overseas offices. Its products include Milkita, a popular confectionery brand, and Lemonilo, an instant noodle variety, according to its website.

The factory's CEO Steven Erwin Wijaya has said about 300 people were present at the factory complex for Saturday's shift.

The search continued on Monday with remaining hotspots and the building's increasingly unstable structure posing safety risks for rescuers, according to Al Amrad, head of the Banten search and rescue agency.

He told reporters 29 people were confirmed safe, five of whom were hospitalised. Rescuers had so far taken away 24 body bags containing body parts but authorities on the ground could not immediately confirm the death toll, he said.

The intensity of the fire meant recovered victims were unidentifiable via visual inspection, with efforts ongoing to collect DNA samples from relatives, a process that could take weeks, police official Wahyu Hidayati said.

data.title: Leapmotor's Shares Sharply Lower After Third-Quarter Profitability Weakness
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Shares of Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology fell sharply, after the Chinese automaker's gross profit margin declined in the third quarter.

Its shares dropped 14% to 26.18 Hong Kong dollars early Monday, sharper than the benchmark Hang Seng Index's 0.5% fall.

Leapmotor's decline came after the automaker said its gross profit margin fell to 10.9% in the third quarter, compared with 12.6% in the second quarter and 14.5% a year earlier. Higher material and freight costs weighed on profitability.

Jefferies analysts expect a modest recovery in the company's gross profit margin in the fourth quarter, as memory-chip prices remain high, they said in a note.

Leapmotor's third-quarter revenue rose 63% to 31.7 billion yuan, equivalent to $4.75 billion. However, its net profit plunged to 40 million yuan from 150 million yuan a year earlier despite a record delivery volume of 310,052 units during the period. The company attributed its lower net profit to weaker profitability per vehicle.

Like many of its Chinese peers, Leapmotor faces subdued domestic demand. Sales in foreign markets could offset weakness at home, Jefferies analysts said, adding that the company's overseas profitability could strengthen next year.

The company's vehicle production in overseas markets will likely give it an upper hand in hedging against tariff risks compared with its Chinese peers, they added.

Write to Jiahui Huang at jiahui.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Gold rises from 14-month low as markets await US inflation data
data.description:
Key points:
  • US PCE data due on Wednesday
  • Traders price in 93% chance of a Fed rate hike in December
  • Fed's Cook says current US policy rate not high enough to tackle inflation

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold regained some ground on Monday after falling to a 14-month low last week, as investors weighed Federal Reserve commentary and looked to upcoming US inflation data for fresh clues on the trajectory of interest rates.

Spot gold climbed 2% to $3,603.77 per ounce by 0332 GMT. Bullion declined about 9% last week, its steepest weekly decline since March.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.5% to $3,603.20.

"The sell-off in tech stocks and the expectations of weaker economic activity because of the weaker AI boom has led the markets to reprice the path forward for US interest rates which has provided gold with some fundamental support," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

US stock futures rose on Monday while authorities scrambled to shore up sliding stock markets in Asia, after a wipeout last week for the tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

Markets are currently pricing in a 93% chance of an interest rate hike at the central bank's policy meeting in December, down from about a 100% probability last week, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Lower odds of higher interest rates reduce the opportunity cost of holding bullion, enhancing the appeal of the non-yielding asset.

"Despite a modest rebound in early trading today, we still need to be cautious to call a bottom in gold. We also cannot rule out further forced liquidation if volatility in equity markets persists," said Dilin Wu, research strategist at Pepperstone.

Meanwhile, Fed Governor Lisa Cook made a case on Friday for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank's current policy rate was not high enough to deal with inflation levels she viewed with "great concern."

Market participants now await the US Personal Consumption Expenditures data due on Wednesday, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate.

Among other metals, spot silver climbed 2.4% to $42.15 per ounce, platinum gained 0.8% to $1,309.86 and palladium rose 0.2% to $894.58.

data.title: India's food regulator finds sample of Bisleri water to be unsafe
data.description:
India’s food safety regulator has found a sample of Bisleri International’s packaged drinking water unsafe and said it would initiate legal proceedings, in a setback for the country’s best-known bottled water brand.

The sample, collected from Bisleri's premises, did not meet prescribed limits on bromate, a chemical formed as a by-product of certain disinfection processes, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said in a social media post on Sunday.

Bisleri said a sample collected from its Goa facility last year showed bromate levels of 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre, but further independent testing arranged by the company showed the chemical was within prescribed limits.

"Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls...and will continue to cooperate with FSSAI (the regulator) to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process," the company said on Monday.

After Bisleri appealed against an initial finding, a separate laboratory also found the sample unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons, or PAHs, the regulator said.

Bisleri competes with PepsiCo's Aquafina and Coca-Cola's Kinley in India's packaged drinking water market, valued at $3.6 billion in 2025, according to Persistence Market Research.

India's food regulator has stepped up enforcement against major brands this year, including legal action against Nestle over a baby food sample it found substandard in September.

data.title: Indian shares open higher on foreign inflows as AI trade reversal continues
data.description:
Indian shares opened higher on Monday, extending a four-week winning streak, as foreign investors continued to buy stocks in Asia's third-largest economy amid easing oil prices and a global selloff in AI-linked stocks.

The Nifty 50 rose 0.50% to 25,929.15 and the Sensex edged 0.6% higher to 84,421.97, as of 9:15 a.m. IST.

Both benchmarks are now trading less than 1% lower for the year, helped by resurgence in foreign inflows over the last four weeks.

Foreign investors net bought Indian shares worth 103.08 billion rupees ($1.11 billion) on Friday, as per provisional data.

They have invested a record $13 billion so far in November, reducing year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion, below the record outflows in 2025.

Fifteen of the 16 major sectors advanced at the open. The broader small-caps and mid-caps gained 0.2% each.

MSCI's broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was down 1%, as investors questioned the massive, largely debt-funded spending on data centres to power AI models.

data.title: EU Inks Deals With Indonesia to Cut Tariffs, Catalyze Investment
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

The European Union signed ambitious agreements with Indonesia that eliminate most tariffs on goods between the two sides, aiming to will deliver billions in economic benefits.

Brussels announced the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with Indonesia on Saturday, more than 10 years after negotiations began. The parties also inked an Investment Protection Agreement to encourage bilateral flows.

"EU-Indonesia trade and investment has vast untapped potential," said Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission.

Duties on main EU export products, including meat and dairy, will be removed, while existing tariffs on cars, machinery, chemicals and pharmaceuticals will be cut.

According to Indonesia's Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, about 90% of tariffs on EU-bound exports to the EU will be removed, while others will be gradually reduced over 3 to 15 years or benefit from tariff-rate quotas.

The preferential access is expected to make Indonesian exports--particularly footwear, textiles and processed commodities--more competitive in the European market, it added.

The pacts open "new doors for businesses," bolstering cooperation in sectors like agri-food and advanced manufacturing, said EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič.

With the deals in place, EU shipments to Indonesia are projected to increase by nearly 40% over 15 years, while Indonesian exports of goods and services to the bloc are expected to rise by more than 14%.

"This will boost economic growth," the commission said, projecting that the EU's gross domestic product will be 16 billion euros higher and Indonesia's 27 billion euros higher, or $17.55 billion and $29.62 billion respectively.

Lowered trade barriers and streamlined investment frameworks will unlock opportunities for European businesses and farmers in Indonesia's market of 280 million consumers, the commission said. EU exporters stand to save over $650 million in annual duties.

Another key benefit for the EU is access to Indonesia's vast resources of materials like nickel and cobalt that are used in everything from electric vehicles to jet engines.

The agreement will give manufacturers stable, predictable access to critical resources, strengthening the trading bloc's supply chain against shocks, the commission said.

"It also provides an export duty-free quota for crude palm and palm kernel oil, both of which are strategic inputs for EU industries," it added.

Recent supply-chain disruptions stemming from wars and other shocks have underlined the need for countries to build up resilience via trade alliances and diversification.

The EU has already concluded agreements with Singapore and Vietnam, and is in ongoing trade negotiations with Thailand and the Philippines.

The investment and economic partnerships struck with Indonesia require the European Parliament's consent and Indonesia's internal ratification. They are expected to be provisionally applied in early 2027.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 21 paise higher at 92.46 per dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened higher on November 23, as a deepening technology rout has strengthened expectations of sustained foreign buying in local equities.

The rupee opened with a gain of 21 paise at 92.46 per dollar, compared with previous close of 92.67.

According to Finrex, the Indian Rupee is set to open higher at 93.54 this morning as we would be seeing FPIs inflows worth approximately USD 1 billion on Friday getting sold off today. With most markets in a down mode, India has been in the driver’s seat in respect of equities and accordingly the rupee has been gaining with a 1.6% gain last week.

The dollar index was constant at 103.76 while Brent oil was at $ 91.05 for the January contract, giving Indian equities and rupee the upside momentum.

RBI has not been buying dollars while all of oil demand is getting absorbed from the FPI inflows and balance is getting sold off in the market keeping rupee appreciated. Exporters to sell the intraday upside they get in the pair while importers can buy the dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Chinese yuan emerging as the strongest performer, rising 0.31 percent, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which gained 0.13 percent, and the South Korean won, which edged up 0.08 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar also posted marginal gains of 0.03 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Japanese yen was the worst performer, declining 0.19 percent, followed by the Philippine peso, which fell 0.16 percent, and the Indonesian rupiah, which slipped 0.09 percent. The Thai baht also edged lower by 0.04 percent.

The dollar eased off its highest level in more than a year and a half at the start of Asian trade on Monday, as investor confidence recovered after a selloff last week and traders pared bets that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 103.80, retreating from its highest levels since April 2025.
